text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Costs of the 1998 Lisbon Expo World Fair have exceeded earlier estimates by 10 percent, according to a budget prepared by the new commissioner Torres Campos. Next week, Presidency Minister Antonio Vitorino will approve spending cuts.

- The privatisation of EDP-Electricidade de Portugal was postponed from May to the middle of June in order not to coincide with the privatisation of France Telecom in May, Under-Secretary for Industry and Energy, Jose Penedos, said.

- Banco Universo, an in-store bank belonging to the Sonae retail group, was launched yesterday and has begun a campaign to attract savings. Branches will be located in Modelo and Continente hypermarkets.
- Portugal's biggest trade union group, the CGTP, received 10 billion escudos from the European Union between 1987 and 1995. Some of the funds were used for professional training.
- The World Jewish Congress, drawing from British documentation from World War Two, said Portugal received $139 million of Nazi gold and that the Portuguese government knew about its origin.
- Fatima Roque, outspoken former UNITA politician, was invited to take part in Angola's national unity government as Minister of Science and Technology.
- The government will change the board of gas group Transgas to make the company more dynamic, an Economy Ministry source said. Elias da Costa, the company's president, will keep his job.
